title: Redwood Inference — Sales Demo Deck Outline (Working v0.7)
content:
Working notes for the canonical demo deck. This is NOT final copy. Goal is to be usable by AEs/SEs with minimal improvisation + clear optional modules.

Audience assumptions:
- Default: product+platform buyer (ML platform lead + app engineer in the room). Security reviewer may join later.
- Demo length targets: 30 mins (standard), 20 mins (exec skim), 45 mins (deep dive / platform).

Hard requirements (demo env constraints):
- Must work even if dashboards were empty 10 mins ago → always run synthetic traffic job before call (or have backup screenshots).
- Must be stable across model catalog changes → pinned demo routes + safe fallback.
- Must avoid customer data → all org/project names + logs + traces are synthetic.

Deck structure options:
A) PLG → Enterprise narrative (default for devtools / AI-native / mixed rooms)
B) Enterprise-first narrative (default for regulated / procurement-led / security-heavy rooms)

--------------------------------------------------------------------
A) Slide order: PLG → Enterprise (default)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
S1 — Title: “Redwood Inference: production-grade LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments”
- Subtitle: “Latency. Cost. Reliability. One runtime.”
Speaker notes:
- Quick intros + confirm time.
- “We’ll show a short live workflow in the Console + API calls. If anything flakes, we have backup screenshots but we try to run it live.”
TODO:
- Confirm exact tagline + approved headline from Marketing.

S2 — Agenda (30 min)
- 2 min: context / what we’re solving
- 5 min: platform overview
- 18 min: live demo (API → economics → reliability → observability)
- 5 min: security/deployment modes + next steps
Speaker notes:
- Ask 1 discovery Q before proceeding: “What matters most today: latency, unit cost, reliability, or deployment constraints?”
TODO:
- Add 20-min and 45-min variants as footnotes.

S3 — Problem slide: “Model choice isn’t the bottleneck anymore. Serving is.”
Bullets:
- Teams lose time on: chasing latency regressions, GPU capacity planning, routing/fallback, observability gaps
- LLM costs are dominated by serving + tokens, not training
- Every environment is different (hosted, dedicated, VPC, on-prem)
Speaker notes:
- Keep it factual; don’t dunk on DIY.
- Bridge: “We focus on making inference predictable in production.”
TODO:
- Insert one simple ‘symptom’ story (429s, empty dashboards, rollout surprise) that matches our own demo failure modes (meta but relatable).

S4 — Why now: “Open models + fast hardware cycles = operational churn”
Bullets:
- Model catalogs shift weekly
- Hardware/optimizations shift quarterly
- Reliability expectations are now ‘core product’ not ‘nice-to-have’
Speaker notes:
- 30 seconds. Don’t overdo the market slide.

S5 — What is Redwood (one slide overview)
- Hosted API (fast start)
- Dedicated capacity (predictable throughput + isolation)
- Private/VPC/on-prem options (regulated)
- Console (cost/latency/quality + rollouts)
- Optimize toolkit (batching/caching/quantization recommendations)
Speaker notes:
- “One API surface, consistent tooling across environments.”
TODO:
- Decide whether “Optimize” is the right product name in customer-facing narrative (field feedback: can confuse).

S6 — Differentiators: “Production economics + reliability controls built in”
Bullets:
- Token-level latency/cost breakdowns
- Continuous batching + caching (with safe toggles)
- Routing policies + fallbacks to keep apps online
- Rollouts: pin versions, canary/A-B, auto fallback
Speaker notes:
- Set up what they’ll see in the live demo.
- Avoid deep kernel talk; keep it at “controls + observability.”
TODO:
- Add proof points/benchmarks once approved for external share.

S7 — Live demo setup (what we’re about to do)
- “We’ll build an LLM feature like an app team would”
- Scenario modules:
  1) API: streaming chat + structured output + tool calling
  2) Economics: batching/caching impact on $ and p95 latency
  3) Reliability: fallback routing (model variant / region)
  4) Observability: traces, errors, rollouts view
Speaker notes:
- “We’ll do this in a demo tenant with synthetic traffic so you can see real dashboards.”
TODO:
- Add a ‘backup mode’ callout: “If live Console is slow, jump to screenshots.”

S8 — Demo Module 1: API (Developer-first)
On-slide bullets (minimal):
- Streaming chat completions
- Structured outputs (JSON schema)
- Tool/function calling
- Retries + idempotency patterns
Speaker notes (SE-led):
- Show code snippet (Python or TS) + one live request.
- Emphasize: same endpoint across environments; pin model version in route config.
Demo steps (speaker notes):
1) Open demo app / snippet.
2) Run streaming chat.
3) Run structured output example (e.g., “extract fields into JSON”).
4) Trigger tool call (e.g., “lookup policy doc” / “fetch order status” with mocked tool response).
TODO:
- Confirm canonical tool-calling example; needs to be compelling but not risky.

S9 — (Optional) The “route” abstraction (1 slide, very fast)
- “Routes let you pin model versions + set policies without rewriting app code”
- Pin + rollout controls
Speaker notes:
- Use only if the room cares about platform controls.
TODO:
- Add screenshot of Routes config page (Design is producing annotated images).

S10 — Demo Module 2: Production economics (the money slide)
On-slide bullets:
- Toggle batching/caching policy
- See impact: tokens/sec, p50/p95 latency, $/1k tokens
- Token-level breakdown: prompt vs completion vs overhead
Speaker notes:
- Avoid making this a benchmark contest.
- “We give you levers + visibility; you choose the tradeoff.”
Demo steps:
1) In Console: show cost/latency dashboard for the demo project.
2) Flip batching policy preset (safe preset).
3) Re-run a fixed prompt set / traffic burst.
4) Point to change in latency/cost charts.
TODO:
- Ensure synthetic traffic generator creates visible deltas (ENG-4833).
- Decide if we show quantization recs here or keep for appendix.

S11 — Demo Module 3: Reliability / graceful degradation
On-slide bullets:
- Fallback routing to compatible variants
- Regional failover story
- Capacity-aware routing (avoid 429 surprises)
Speaker notes:
- “Outages happen. The question is whether your app returns something sensible.”
Demo steps:
1) Show routing policy page (pinned model + allowed fallbacks).
2) Trigger a controlled failure (simulate capacity constraint / region toggle).
3) Show request still completes + annotate response header/metadata indicating fallback.
4) Show audit trail / event in Console.
TODO:
- Keep the failure controlled and reversible; avoid doing anything that risks the tenant.
- Confirm exact demo-safe failure mechanism with Mina/Ravi.

S12 — Demo Module 4: Observability (Console tour)
On-slide bullets:
- Per-route latency/cost + token breakdown
- Traces + error analysis
- Rollouts view: canary/A-B + auto fallback policy
Speaker notes:
- The ‘aha’ is: “You can debug and manage inference like a real production service.”
Demo steps:
1) Open dashboard overview (last 24h + last 15m toggles).
2) Click into a route → show latency distribution + cost breakdown.
3) Open a trace sample (show tool call / streaming timing if available).
4) Open rollouts view (show canary percentage + rollback).
TODO:
- Call out which pages are stable enough to demo. Avoid flaky screens.

S13 — Deployment modes (unified story)
- Hosted: fastest start
- Dedicated: reserved capacity, isolation, predictable throughput
- Private: VPC / on-prem options, customer-managed networking
Speaker notes:
- Tie back to: “same runtime + same operational controls.”
- If customer asks: “What changes between modes?” answer: primarily networking + isolation + control plane placement.
TODO:
- Add a simple architecture diagram (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) with consistent terminology.

S14 — Enterprise/security (narrative + screenshots)
Bullets:
- SSO/SAML
- RBAC
- Audit logs
- Retention controls
- KMS/HSM integrations (where applicable)
Speaker notes:
- “We can share the security FAQ links after the call; we’ll keep this high-level here.”
- If they want depth, offer a follow-up security review call.
TODO:
- Confirm safe-to-show audit log screenshot content (no sensitive fields).

S15 — ROI framing / when customers choose Redwood
- “When unit costs + reliability start impacting roadmap”
- Common triggers: high traffic, multi-team platform standardization, regulated data, need for SLAs
Speaker notes:
- Keep it credible. Avoid hard ROI numbers unless approved.
TODO:
- Pull 2–3 proof points from “customer-proof-points-for-demo” doc and mark what’s external-safe.

S16 — Close / next steps
Options:
- “We can spin up a POC with your prompts and success metrics”
- “We can do a dedicated capacity sizing session”
- “We can run a security + architecture review”
Speaker notes:
- Ask: “What would make this a ‘yes’ for you in the next 2–3 weeks?”
TODO:
- Add a simple mutual action plan checklist (MAP) slide for enterprise.

Appendix slides (optional modules)
A1 — API reference: endpoints + SDKs
A2 — Pricing overview (high level): hosted usage-based + Dedicated commits + Private licensing
A3 — Reliability deep dive: routing policy types
A4 — Quality monitoring / evals: prompt sets, regression alerts
A5 — Private deployment architecture (VPC / on-prem)
A6 — FAQ: data retention/residency, data usage, logging defaults


--------------------------------------------------------------------
B) Slide order: Enterprise-first (regulated / procurement-led)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
This order front-loads security + deployment constraints to earn the right to do the live demo.
Recommended when:
- They start with “Do you support VPC / residency / audit logs?”
- They have a security reviewer on the invite
- They’ve been burned by vendor ‘handwaving’ on controls

B-order (suggested):
1 Title
2 Agenda (explicitly call out security module early)
3 Deployment modes (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
4 Enterprise/security (SSO/RBAC/audit logs/retention)
5 Reliability controls (fallback, pinning, rollouts) — high level
6 Live demo setup
7 API module (streaming/structured/tool calling)
8 Observability module
9 Production economics module
10 Close / next steps
Appendix: pricing, deeper architecture

Speaker note for B-order transition:
- “Now that we’ve covered whether Redwood fits your constraints, let’s show how the team actually uses it day-to-day.”


--------------------------------------------------------------------
“Skip list” for a 20-minute exec demo
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Goal: show only ‘why’, 1–2 live moments, and credible enterprise posture.
Recommended set:
- Keep: Title, Problem, What is Redwood, Live API moment (streaming + structured output), 1 Console dashboard view (cost/latency), Deployment modes, Security (1 slide), Close.
- Skip: Detailed route slide, deep rollouts view, deep reliability trigger (unless it’s their #1 concern).


--------------------------------------------------------------------
Open questions / TODOs (parking lot)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
1) Naming: keep “Optimize” or talk as “cost/performance toolkit” (field feedback says “Optimize” can sound like a separate product tax).
2) Proof points: need approved benchmark ranges + caveats (marketing requested consistency; eng needs sign-off).
3) Live reliability demo: confirm the safest trigger + the exact on-screen evidence that fallback occurred (header? event log? both).
4) Console tour: identify the 3 most stable pages. Avoid anything that can show empty state unexpectedly.
5) Dedicated vs Hosted messaging: need crisp one-liner to avoid pricing confusion (“Dedicated = reserved GPUs + predictable throughput; Hosted = pay-as-you-go”).
6) EMEA variant: add one slide or speaker note emphasizing data residency + region selection.


--------------------------------------------------------------------
Notes from recent field feedback (raw)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
- Customers love tool calling + structured outputs, but the example has to be ‘real’ (not a toy calculator).
- Demos break most often on: quota/429s, dashboards empty, streaming disconnect in specific region.
- The story drags if we over-explain kernels/engine internals. Show levers + outcomes.

Owner checklist before sending to Design for v1:
- Finalize slide titles + max 3 bullets per slide.
- Add explicit ‘who’s talking’ (AE vs SE) in speaker notes.
- Tag each slide as MUST/OPTIONAL.
- Create a backup screenshot list with filenames + where to store them.

End.
